memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: 36-year-old male driver reports intermittent abdominal bloating and diarrhoea, occasional spinning sensation on lying down, and persistent worry and restlessness.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/78, weight 78 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 27.0 (obese). Abdomen soft, non-tender. Neurological: Dix-Hallpike elicits vertigo with torsional nystagmus right side. No focal deficits.
IMPRESSION: 1) Irritable bowel syndrome, diarrhoea-predominant. 2) Benign positional vertigo, right posterior canal. 3) Generalised anxiety disorder, moderate. Plan to screen for coeliac disease and baseline labs.
ARRANGEMENTS: Prescribe mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS; betahistine 16 mg BD, meclizine 25 mg SOS; escitalopram 5 mg OD, buspirone 5 mg BD. Order CBC, stool routine, tTG-IgA, Dix-Hallpike, audiometry, GAD-7, TSH, Hb. Advise regular meals, hydration, vestibular rehab exercises, and daily walk. Return if: worsening abdominal pain with blood, vomiting, severe vertigo with falls, panic attacks, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports fewer loose stools, only occasional urgency after meals; vertigo episodes reduced to once per week, lasting <30 seconds; anxiety feels better but still experiences tension.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/80, weight 77.5 kg, BMI 26.8 (overweight). Abdomen non-tender. Dix-Hallpike now negative.
IMPRESSION: IBS improving; BPPV resolved; GAD moderate. Continue current therapy, increase escitalopram for residual anxiety.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS; betahistine 16 mg BD, meclizine 25 mg SOS; increase escitalopram to 10 mg OD, buspirone 5 mg BD unchanged. Advise high‑fibre diet, regular aerobic activity, and continue vestibular exercises. Repeat CBC, TSH, GAD-7 in 3 months. Return if: rectal bleeding, severe abdominal pain, new vertigo with falls, worsening panic, or fever >39°C.

memories.text:
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: After a long‑haul trip, patient reports increased bloating, 3‑4 loose stools daily, two episodes of vertigo lasting a minute each, and heightened worry with difficulty sleeping.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/82, weight 79 kg, BMI 27.3 (obese). Abdomen mildly tender in left lower quadrant. Dix-Hallpike elicits mild vertigo.
IMPRESSION: IBS flare; recurrent BPPV; anxiety worsened. Adjust medications and reinforce lifestyle.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase mebeverine to 135 mg QID, ispaghula husk to 5 g BID, keep loperamide 2 mg SOS; raise betahistine to 24 mg BD, add meclizine 25 mg BD for prophylaxis; increase escitalopram to 15 mg OD, buspirone to 10 mg BD. Order CBC, stool routine, tTG-IgA, Dix-Hallpike, audiometry, GAD-7, TSH. Advise low‑FODMAP meals during travel, hydration, and continue vestibular rehab. Return if: bloody stools, severe abdominal pain, vertigo with falls, panic attack, or fever >39°C.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports stable bowel pattern (2‑3 formed stools/day), no vertigo episodes in past 6 weeks, and anxiety feels much better with occasional mild worry.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/80, weight 78 kg, BMI 27.0 (obese). Abdomen soft, non‑tender.
IMPRESSION: IBS in remission; BPPV resolved; GAD mild. Consider tapering medications if symptoms remain stable.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS; betahistine 16 mg BD, meclizine 25 mg SOS; escitalopram 15 mg OD, buspirone 10 mg BD. Advise maintain high‑fibre diet, regular exercise, and stress‑reduction techniques. Repeat CBC, TSH, GAD-7 in 3 months. Return if: rectal bleeding, severe abdominal pain, new vertigo, worsening anxiety, or fever >39°C.
